meta.question: What is the MECHANISM of the secondary-cascade ionisation deficit (E20: 216.9 vs 313.6)? Is it the untracked tertiary cascade (secondary.wgsl absorbs tertiaries in place)?
meta.method: Counted Geant4 dna.root ionisations (flag 13) by cascade generation using step trackID+parentID: gen1=trackID==1, gen2=trackID>1 & parentID==1, gen3+=parentID>1. Compared to our model (tracks gen1+gen2, absorbs gen3+).

summary.headline: The cascade deficit is 80% the UNTRACKED TERTIARY+ CASCADE (gen3+ = 77.2 ions/primary that our secondary.wgsl absorbs in place rather than tracking) + 20% a small gen2 under-ionisation (216.9 vs 236.4). gen1 (primary) matches Geant4 exactly.
summary.fix: Emit tertiary electrons from secondary ionisations (W_sec>cutoff) into sec_buf instead of depositing in place, and let the Phase B wavefront grow to process them (dispatch.ts re-reads sec_n). Recovers ~77 of the 97 missing ionisations -> total ~489 vs Geant4 509 (0.96x). It is a deliberate architectural simplification (depth-2 cascade), not a physics error — but it is the fixable root of the cascade deficit.
